propositions: Code review currently has no detection language for fail-open checks whose pass/absent result is indistinguishable from the check never running, a defect pattern that appeared 9+ times in production

The fail-open antipattern occurs in two populations: test-oracle code (absence assertions on subprocess/file output with no liveness check) and shipped-code error-handling (silent lookup misses, unchecked returncodes, pgrep self-matches)

The criterion language must broaden to cover both passing and failing definite results, since a broken instrument can produce false alarms (absence where presence exists) as well as false passes, and both are indistinguishable from producer failure

Fail-open detection language must be added to the existing tests and error-handling criteria (per operator ruling) rather than creating a new criterion, with additions to their rubric files and calibration via 18 eval cases (9 pre-fix must-fire, 9 post-fix must-be-silent)

The remediation litmus requires naming every world in which a check produces any definite result; if 'the producer never ran' or 'emitted nothing' is among them, the check cannot distinguish its verdict from its own failure
